text:
perf-alert-bot: ALERT p99 > SLO on prod-east for model=redwood-ggml-13b — observed 2.3s, SLO=1.2s. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/kkk/perf :rotating_light:

maria: seeing repeated p99 spikes from ~14:02 UTC, p50 fine. pods show pulsing behaviour. tagging @devon @lee for perf deep-dive.

devon: grabbing profiler traces now. initial hypothesis: kernel selector rapidly toggles between optimized_attention and gemm_fallback depending on instantaneous batch shape.

devon: sample kernel log:
```
[14:03:01] kernel_choice: seq=1536, batch_tok=4800 -> optimized_attention (14.2ms)
[14:03:03] kernel_choice: seq=3072, batch_tok=2400 -> gemm_fallback (58.0ms)
[14:03:05] kernel_choice: seq=1536, batch_tok=4800 -> optimized_attention (13.9ms)
```

lee: that flip is classic microbatch headroom oscillation. arrival_rate jitter causes heuristic to shrink/grow and we keep falling into slower kernels mid-run.

anika: adding that KV cache churn spikes are co-timed. when a long prompt arrives (>>2k tokens) we see lots of new KV entries then a flurry of short generations that evict older entries. evictions correlate with latency tails.

maria: timeline: long prompt at 14:02:40, tool calls inline at 14:02:45, then p99 climbs across pods around 14:03:10. devon, share kv counters?

devon: kv snapshot (short):
```
kv_capacity=1.2M
kv_hit_rate=0.69
kv_evictions_min=48
kv_evictions_peak=198
avg_kv_item=1.1kB
```

lee: traces show a repeated pattern: model emits partial span -> router invokes external tool sync -> external latency ~200-400ms -> model resumes and emits next chunk -> repeat. Each resume has variable seq_len and forces kernel re-eval and KV state changes.

anika: so two problems: (1) long prompts push seq_len into slower kernels, (2) tool-call fragmentation prevents stable microbatching and thrashes KV cache. Together they create tail events.

maria: proposed repro/mitigation steps:
- replay recorded trace for long-prompt + tool-loop
- conservative kernel pin for seq_len <= 4096 on a small canary
- increase microbatch minimum tokens and add hysteresis to growth/shrink
- temporarily bump kv cache capacity on canary pods

devon: quick canary: pinned optimized_attention up to 4096 + kv bump on 3 canary pods. result: p99 dropped from 2.3s -> 1.0s on canary, sawtooth disappeared. profiler:
```
lat_p50=90ms
lat_p95=220ms
lat_p99=1.0s
kernels: optimized_attention 94%, fallback 6%
```

lee: pinning helps but it's a blunt approach. longer term we need a smoother microbatch controller. current logic (pseudo):
```
if est_latency(batch_tokens) > SLO:
  shrink_headroom()
else:
  grow_headroom()
```
That binary toggle flips under noisy arrivals.

anika: suggestion: use EWMA for batch_token estimate, add hysteresis bands and a min-dwell time (e.g., 300ms) before adjusting batch window. also mark requests with tool_call=true as potential blockers so router treats them differently.

maria: agreed. action items:
- devon: add kernel-flip telemetry (flip_count per minute) + attach to pod metrics (PR incoming)
- lee: implement tool-call detector in router and isolate these requests into separate queue or lower-co-batching priority
- anika: create SLI for kv_eviction_rate and alert threshold
- infra-bot: roll canary (kv bump + kernel pin) for 30m and report metrics

devon: PR link for telemetry: https://git.internal/r/repo/commit/abcd123 (adds kernel_flip counter and microbatch stats).

lee: router change idea: if request has tool_call=true OR carries external_future token, route to an isolation queue that aims for single-request handling (no aggressive co-batching). easiest path to remove fragmentation.

anika: also we should include quantized model variants in tests — q4 paths magnify kernel differences. run replay across float/quant variants.

maria: devon, can you paste a short profile for the worst-case trace?

devon: bad-trace profile snippet:
```
trace_id=zzzz
total_gen=1.9s
 - attention_opt: 0.13s x 10
 - matmul_fallback: 0.47s x 3
 - ext_wait_http: 0.31s x 5
kv_evict_time: 0.28s
```

maria: infra-bot, start canary now.

infra-bot: canary started: prod-east-canary-1..3. will report back in 10m.

devon: note for follow-up: our SLO model needs to account for external-blocking latency. heuristics that optimize for average arrival rates but ignore external waits produce bad tails.

lee: I'll spin up a short design doc for router isolation patterns and propose a microbatch controller with EWMA + hysteresis. will include small sim harness and replay results.

anika: creating incident ticket INC-2026-342 and adding kv_eviction SLI + dashboard.

maria: excellent. if canary looks stable we'll roll the kernel pin + kv bump while we implement heuristic improvements. keep posting perf graphs and PRs in this thread. :eyes:

devon: quick note: we should add a unit test that simulates alternating long-short arrival patterns and ensures no frequent resizing. I'll add to runtime/tests/microbatch_robustness.py.

maria: thanks all — monitor and update. end of thread.
